title: Arithmetic Conjectures for Beilinson–Bloch Heights
subtitle: Central classes, positivity, and integral Northcott
summary: A hierarchical conjectural package for products of curves, with the distinction between real positivity, integral discreteness, and varying fields made explicit.
evidence: Open arithmetic targets and explicitly conditional implications. The height axioms are hypotheses, not consequences of publication.
html:
1. Introduction

The expected positivity of Beilinson–Bloch heights is an arithmetic Hodge–Riemann principle. A Northcott property is stronger: it asks for finiteness of integral cycle classes of bounded degree and height. Even a positive quadratic form does not give this finiteness unless the integral classes are arithmetically discrete. Allowing the field of definition to vary adds a further descent problem.

For products of curves, tensor Chow projectors separate these questions. The all-h1h^1h1 part of a subproduct carries a central height precisely when its dimension is 2c−12c-12c−1 in codimension ccc. The other parts are responsible for arithmetic Lefschetz. Within the central part, curve correspondences separate a Néron–Tate summand and its residual Griffiths quotient. This paper formulates the resulting conjectures and organizes the arithmetic inputs to their study. The complete reduction proofs are given in the companion manuscript [1].

These conjectures are expressed within the Bloch–Beilinson and arithmetic standard-conjecture framework. The arithmetic Lefschetz and primitive positivity statements are those recorded in [6, Conjecture 2.3.1]. The purpose of the formulation here is to specify the residual objects, their integral images and the exact implications connecting the different arithmetic questions.

5. A proof programme and its arithmetic obstacles

The reduction theorem provides two complementary routes. One seeks the three central assertions directly. The other constructs arithmetic detectors for the residual quotient and then proves integral and field-of-definition control.

5.1. The geometric and central steps

The first target is Conjecture 1.3. The tensor Chow decomposition gives an exact test: a nonzero off-central core would produce a misplaced Lefschetz string. A proof must therefore eliminate the core in the rational Chow group, rather than merely its cohomological realization.

The next target is the algebraic kernel in Conjecture 1.4. The projector construction already identifies it as RSAS,ER_SA_{S,E}RS​AS,E​, and adjunction places it in the full central height radical. Establishing its vanishing is a separate arithmetic cycle statement. Once it vanishes, the visible Néron–Tate factor has all the required fixed-field and bounded-degree finiteness properties.

For the residual factor, real positivity is an initial target. It supplies Cauchy–Schwarz and, together with the algebraic kernel statement, central nondegeneracy. The primitive sum-of-squares identity transfers these consequences uniformly to every degree of the product.

5.2. A detector-to-Northcott route

For each fixed finite E/F0E/F_0E/F0​, the sequence of inputs is:

  1. Prove scalar-extended injectivity of one residual regulator. The finite-dimensional cohomological target then gives finite rational rank.

  2. Prove one common denominator bound for the integral image, for example through the all-prime saturation condition (3.1). Alternatively, combine a finite Kummer quotient with a positive height gap.

  3. Establish real residual positivity. Together with the common lattice, this gives fixed-field Northcott.

  4. Control the ramification of minimal class fields in bounded degree and height. The trace criterion then gives bounded-degree Northcott.

The alternatives in the second step have different arithmetic content. All-prime saturation compares integral cohomology across coefficient primes. The height-gap route instead requires a uniform positive lower bound on nonzero integral classes over the fixed field.

Under real positivity, scalar detection and the almost-everywhere lattice comparison for every finite E/F0E/F_0E/F0​, the first three steps establish fixed-field Northcott. Adding Conjecture 4.1 proves Conjecture 1.5. Alternatively, a finite Kummer quotient and a genuine gap over every fixed field, together with real positivity and Conjecture 4.1, give the same conclusion without a preliminary finite-rank assumption. Finally, Conjecture 1.3 and Conjecture 1.4 and Theorem 2.1 give the product programme.

The local-to-global construction of a height system and these arithmetic properties meet at Definition 1.1. A construction of local Green forms must supply the global pairing, adjunction and curve normalization before the arithmetic reductions apply. The present programme starts from that explicitly stated height system; its subsequent tasks concern vanishing, positivity, integral discreteness and fields of cycle classes.

abstractHtml: We formulate an arithmetic programme for height pairings on the homologically trivial Chow groups of products of curves. Exact Chow projectors reduce arithmetic hard Lefschetz to off-central vanishing and reduce primitive integral Northcott to two central assertions: injectivity of the algebraic Abel–Jacobi map and Northcott on a residual Griffiths quotient. The latter assertion contains real positivity but also requires integral and varying-field information. We separate the proposed arithmetic inputs into scalar detection by continuous étale cohomology, a common rational lattice, and ramification control for the minimal fields of cycle classes. The stated implications specify where each input enters.
